mainTopic: מקדיש versus מתכפר for חומש and תמורה, and the new משנה on substituting limbs and fetuses
overview: The גמרא finishes a question about when a person who redeems a holy animal does not add another חומש. It then asks a harder version of that question and leaves it as תיקו. Next, רמי בר חמא asks about one person who dedicates an animal for another person's atonement: who adds the חומש, and who can make a תמורה? רבא learns from a פסוק that the מקדיש adds the חומש. He also shows that the תמורה must follow the מתכפר, or else a ציבור or שותפין could make one. A further proof from a נזיר's offering is pushed off. The גמרא then settles both questions with רבי יוחנן's rule, which also says that a person who gives תרומה from his own produce for others chooses the כהן. A new משנה teaches that a תמורה does not work with limbs or fetuses, though רבי יוסי allows a limb for a whole holy animal. The גמרא begins by bringing a מחלוקת between בר פדא and רבי יוחנן on whether a fetus can become holy, and starts to explain why רבי יוחנן's two rulings are both needed; this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second side of the question: maybe any animal with the same holiness is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a question that began earlier. Maybe the rule of not adding another חומש applies to any animal that carries the same holiness, not only to the original animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: for anything with that same holiness, he does not add a fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of a question it began just before this. Maybe the exemption from adding a חומש covers any animal that carries the same קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side of the question limited the exemption to the original body of the animal. This second side makes the type of קדושה the deciding factor, so a different animal holding that same holiness would also be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This brings in the second side of a question.
Holiness, the sacred status of the animal
The extra fifth a person adds when redeeming his own consecrated item

phrases.english: Or perhaps: for anything with that same holiness
he does not add a fifth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כׇּל אוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה אֵינוֹ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question that began before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the exemption from adding another חומש depend on the original body, or on the same type of קדושה?

steps.title: A harder case: the original animal was replaced and changed to a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we say a different animal with the same holiness is exempt. What about the original animal that was replaced by another and changed to an עולה? It is the same body, but it now has a different holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that this other body, since it stands in the same holiness, does not have a fifth added, what about when he gained atonement through another animal, and this one was moved to be an עולה? Does the exemption apply only to the same body with the same holiness, and not to a different holiness? Or perhaps, since it is the same body, he does not add a fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first. It asks about a case where the body stays the same but the type of holiness changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question compared a different body with the same holiness. Here it is the reverse: the original body now has a different holiness, because it became an עולה after the owner gained atonement with another animal. The question is whether the exemption needs both the same body and the same holiness, or whether being the same body is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Body. Here it means the physical animal itself.
He gained atonement through a different animal
It was moved over to become an עולה (a burnt offering)
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two questions. The first was a different body with the same holiness. This one is the same body with a different holiness.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says תיקו. The question stays open with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether being the same body is enough when the holiness has changed. The question is left standing without a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: The question about the original animal that was replaced and changed to an עולה ends with תיקו. We never learn whether the same body alone is enough to exempt it from another חומש.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.title: Who adds the fifth: the one who dedicates or the one who gains atonement?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks about a case where one person dedicates an animal for another person's atonement. When it is redeemed, who adds the חומש?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: does the one who dedicates add the fifth, or does the one who gains atonement add the fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רמי בר חמא asks which of the two people counts as the 'owner' for the rule of adding a חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people are connected to this animal. The מקדיש made it holy, and the מתכפר is the one who gains atonement through it. The question is which of them the rule of the extra fifth follows.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question
The person who dedicates the animal
The person who gains atonement through the offering

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
Does the one who dedicates add the fifth,
or does the one who gains atonement add the fifth?
phrases.notes: Some versions have מכפר in round brackets; the corrected wording is מִתְכַּפֵּר, the person who gains atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מַקְדִּישׁ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about which person the rule of חומש follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the חומש obligation follow the מקדיש or the מתכפר?

steps.title: רבא: the verse says the one who dedicates adds the fifth
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the פסוק 'ואם המקדיש יגאל את ביתו' and learns that the מקדיש adds the חומש, not the מתכפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the verse says, 'And if the one who dedicates will redeem his house.' The one who dedicates, and not the one who gains atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from a פסוק. The פסוק names the מקדיש as the one who adds the fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about adding a fifth uses the word 'המקדיש,' the one who dedicates. Since it says that word, the duty falls on him and not on the מתכפר.

keyTerms.meaning: He will redeem

steps.whatToRemember: For adding the חומש, the person who counts is the מקדיש, not the מתכפר.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says,
"And if the one who dedicates will redeem his house" —
the one who dedicates, and not the one who gains atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's question from a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקדיש adds the חומש, based on the word 'המקדיש' in ויקרא 27:15.

steps.title: Who can make a substitute: the one who dedicates or the one who gains atonement?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks a similar question about תמורה. In the same case, which of the two people can make a substitute animal take on the holiness?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: does the one who dedicates make a תמורה, or does the one who gains atonement make a תמורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks the same kind of question again, this time about the power to make a תמורה. The גמרא is setting up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the חומש follows the מקדיש. The question now is whether the power of תמורה works the same way or follows the מתכפר instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution. Trying to swap a regular animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too.
Has the power to make a substitute

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
Does the one who dedicates make a substitute,
or does the one who gains atonement make a substitute?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מַקְדִּישׁ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to step 4, now about תמורה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the power to make a תמורה belong to the מקדיש or the מתכפר?

steps.title: רבא: if the one who dedicates could substitute, a community or partners could too
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows a problem with saying the מקדיש makes the תמורה. Then a ציבור or שותפין who sent one שליח to dedicate for them would be able to make a תמורה, which the משנה rules out. So the power belongs to the מתכפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if so, we would find a community or partners able to make a substitute, for example where they appointed an agent to dedicate the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by showing what would go wrong if the מקדיש were the one who makes the תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a ציבור or שותפין appoint one שליח to dedicate an animal for them. Then a single person is the מקדיש. If the מקדיש could make a תמורה, a תמורה would work for an offering of a ציבור or of שותפין. But a later משנה teaches that it never does, so the power must follow the מתכפר.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This shows a problem that would follow from an idea.
The community
Partners
An agent sent to act for someone

steps.whatToRemember: The two questions get opposite answers. The חומש follows the מקדיש, but the power to make a תמורה follows the מתכפר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume both questions have the same answer. רבא ties the חומש to the מקדיש, but the תמורה to the מתכפר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that each law can follow a different person. The answer depends on its own source.

phrases.english: Rava said: If so,
we would find a community and partners making a substitute,
phrases.notes: This is a problem because a later משנה says that offerings of a community or of partners can't have a תמורה.

phrases.english: for example, where they appointed an agent to dedicate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, מָצִינוּ צִיבּוּר וְשׁוּתָּפִין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about תמורה by showing what would go wrong with the side of the מקדיש
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מתכפר makes the תמורה. Otherwise a ציבור or שותפין acting through one שליח could make a תמורה, which the משנה rules out.

steps.title: A further proof from the נזיר's offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the words 'besides what his hand can reach' as covering a נזיר whose offering was set aside for him by other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more: רב נחמן said in the name of רב הונא that a ברייתא taught: 'His offering to ה׳ for his נזירות, besides what his hand can reach.' But is a נזיר judged by what he can afford? So how do we read it? 'His offering to ה׳ for his נזירות' means he set it aside from his own animals. 'Besides what his hand can reach' means others set it aside for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The argument brings one more piece of support, a ברייתא about a נזיר. It reads a strange phrase in the פסוק as talking about an offering that other people set aside for the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's offerings are fixed by the Torah and do not change with how rich he is, so 'what his hand can reach' cannot mean his budget. The ברייתא therefore reads it as a second case: an animal someone else set aside for him. This sets up the case of one person dedicating for another person's atonement, which is exactly our question.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to keep away from wine and other things, and brings set offerings when he finishes
What a person can afford (literally, 'what his hand reaches')
His offering
Set aside an animal as a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And furthermore, as Rav Nachman said that Rav Huna said:
It was taught: "His offering to ה׳ for his naziriteship,
besides what his hand can reach".
But is a nazir judged by what he can afford?
So how is this to be understood?
"His offering to ה׳ for his naziriteship" means that he set it aside from his own animals;

phrases.aramaic: ״מִלְּבַד אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יָדוֹ״ — שֶׁהִפְרִישׁוּ לוֹ אֲחֵרִים.
phrases.english: "besides what his hand can reach" means that others set it aside for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to back up the claim from Step 7 that the מתכפר makes the תמורה.
steps.raayaObject: That the מתכפר, not the מקדיש, makes the תמורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading במדבר 6:21 as covering an offering set aside for a נזיר by others

steps.title: What law is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this ruling is for, and says it cannot just be about atonement, because that is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law is this taught? If you say it is about atonement, that is obvious: of course it atones for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical law the ברייתא is teaching. It sets up the next move by ruling out the simple answer, atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone gives the נזיר an animal, it is now his offering, so of course it can bring him כפרה. A ברייתא would not need a פסוק to teach something that obvious. So the גמרא is pushed to look for a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (What is this teaching in practice?)
If you say
Atonement
It is obvious

phrases.english: For what law is this taught?
If you say it is about atonement,
it is obvious that it atones for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical law the ברייתא from Step 8 is teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the ברייתא's case of 'others set it aside for him' is about

steps.title: It must be about תמורה, so we follow the מתכפר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be teaching that the נזיר can make a תמורה even when others set aside his animal, which shows that the מתכפר makes the תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about תמורה, and this is what it means: even when others set it aside for him, he makes a תמורה. Learn from this that we follow the מתכפר!
steps.whatsHappening: Since atonement is too obvious, the גמרא says the ברייתא must be about תמורה. That gives the proof: the person being atoned for has the power of תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the נזיר is the מתכפר, and the 'others' are the מקדיש. If the נזיר can make a תמורה on an animal others dedicated for him, then the power goes with the מתכפר. This answers רמי בר חמא's question the same way רבא did in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
Learn from this
We follow the person who gets the atonement

phrases.english: Rather, it is about substitution,
and this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף כְּשֶׁהִפְרִישׁוּ לוֹ אֲחֵרִים — עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.
phrases.english: Even when others set it aside for him, he makes a substitute.
Learn from this: we follow the one who gets atonement!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9's question by saying the ברייתא is about תמורה, and draws the proof.
steps.raayaObject: The power of תמורה belongs to the מתכפר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the נזיר, read as being about תמורה

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about atonement after all
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא may be about atonement, because without the extra words we might have thought a נזיר can only atone with his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is not about תמורה. And as for what bothered you, that it is a gift they gave him: if the Torah had not added 'besides what his hand can reach,' I would have said it is a special Torah rule. 'His offering' means only his own animal atones, not one from others. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 10. It shows that the ברייתא can be about atonement after all, so it says nothing about תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said atonement was too obvious to need teaching. Here the גמרא answers that it is not obvious: the word 'קרבנו' could have meant only an animal from his own flock counts. The extra words teach that even an animal from others works, so the ברייתא proves nothing about who makes the תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift
The Torah included (added this case)
I would have thought
A Torah rule we follow even without a reason
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבא's answer in Step 7 is wrong. Only this extra proof from the נזיר is pushed off; the question of who makes the תמורה is still settled in the next step.

phrases.english: No, it is not about substitution,
and as for what was difficult for you,
that it is a gift they are giving him,
phrases.notes: This was the reason Step 9 called atonement obvious: once they give it to him, it's his.

phrases.english: if the Merciful One had not included it with
"besides what his hand can reach,"
I would have said it is a decree of the verse:
"his offering" means only from his own does it atone,
but not from that of others;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לְעִנְיַן תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 10 by undoing the reasoning of Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the נזיר ברייתא, not the underlying ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Atonement is not obvious, because 'קרבנו' could have limited it to his own animal, so the ברייתא can be about atonement and not תמורה

steps.title: Final ruling: the מקדיש adds the חומש, the מתכפר makes the תמורה
steps.stepSummary: After the proof was pushed off, the גמרא asks what the final ruling is and brings רבי יוחנן's clear rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the final ruling? Come and hear: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the מקדיש adds the חומש, and the מתכפר makes the תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final הלכה, since the נזיר proof did not hold. It brings רבי יוחנן, who splits the two powers between the two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who dedicated the animal adds the extra fifth when he redeems it, matching רבא in Step 5. The person who gets the atonement is the one who can make a תמורה, matching רבא in Step 7. Now both questions of רמי בר חמא have a firm answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the final ruling on this?

steps.whatToRemember: When one person dedicates an animal for someone else: the מקדיש adds the חומש when redeeming, and the מתכפר is the one who can make a תמורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the different powers over a קרבן can belong to different people: redeeming goes with the one who dedicated it, and תמורה goes with the one it atones for.

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about this?

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Abahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The one who dedicates adds a fifth,
and the one who gets atonement makes a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in Step 11 was pushed off, gives the final הלכה from רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מקדיש adds the חומש, and the מתכפר makes the תמורה.

steps.title: The תרומה giver chooses the recipient
steps.stepSummary: The last part of רבי יוחנן's rule: someone who separates תרומה from his own produce to cover another person's produce keeps the טובת הנאה, meaning the right to choose which כהן gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person gives תרומה from his own produce on behalf of someone else's produce, he is the one who decides which כהן receives it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the clear rule of רבי יוחנן that it brought in step 12. This is the third and last part of that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part moves from קרבנות to תרומה. The right goes to the person whose own produce is actually given, not to the person whose produce is being fixed. So here the one who gives holds the power, much like the מקדיש with the חומש, and not like the מתכפר with the תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates תרומה, the כהן's portion of produce
The small benefit of choosing who receives a gift
From his own produce on behalf of someone else's produce

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's full rule: the מקדיש adds the חומש, the מתכפר makes the תמורה, and someone who gives תרומה from his own produce for others keeps the right to choose the כהן.

phrases.english: One who separates terumah from his own produce for the produce of others —
phrases.notes: This is still רבי יוחנן speaking, continuing the rule from the last step.

phrases.english: the benefit of choosing who receives it is his.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרֵם מִשֶּׁלּוֹ עַל שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rule of רבי יוחנן that was introduced in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Someone who separates תרומה from his own produce for another person's produce has the right to choose the כהן who receives it.

steps.title: The verse behind the תרומה rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the תרומה rule and answers with a פסוק: 'your produce... and you shall give.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is that? Because the פסוק says 'all the tithe of your produce... and you shall give.' The one whose produce it is does the giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the תרומה rule and quotes a פסוק to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties 'your produce' to 'you shall give.' That means the person whose produce is actually handed over is the one who gives, so the choice of recipient is his.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A tithe, a tenth portion of produce

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The verse states:
"All the tithe of your produce..."
"and you shall give," etc.
phrases.notes: The point is that it says 'your produce' and then 'you give.' Whoever's produce it is does the giving and the choosing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from a פסוק for the תרומה rule in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the giver of תרומה from his own produce keeps the טובת הנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 26:12, where 'your produce' is linked to 'and you shall give.'

steps.title: משנה: no substitution between limbs, fetuses, and whole animals
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a תמורה does not work between limbs and fetuses, and not between either of them and whole animals, in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot make a swap of an animal limb for a fetus, a fetus for a limb, a limb or fetus for a whole animal, or a whole animal for a limb or fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching which kinds of exchanges do not create a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal תמורה is one whole animal exchanged for another whole animal. The משנה says that if either side is only a limb or an unborn fetus, the exchange has no effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Make a תמורה, a substitute animal that takes on holiness
Limbs or body parts of an animal
Unborn fetuses inside a mother animal
Whole, complete animals

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שלימים' means whole animals, not the קרבן called שלמים (peace offering).

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One does not make a substitute: not limbs for fetuses,
phrases.notes: The first item is the ordinary animal's part and the second is the holy one, so a non-holy limb is being swapped for a holy fetus.

phrases.english: and not fetuses for limbs,
and not fetuses or limbs for whole animals,
and not whole animals for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְמִירִין, לֹא אֵבָרִין בְּעוּבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה does not take effect when either side of the exchange is a limb or a fetus.

steps.title: רבי יוסי allows a limb for a whole animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees in one direction: a non-holy limb exchanged for a whole holy animal does work, but a whole animal exchanged for a holy limb does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: you can swap a limb for a whole holy animal, but not a whole animal for a holy limb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his own opinion, which partly disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי agrees that a whole animal swapped for a holy limb does nothing. But when the holy side is a whole animal and the ordinary side is a limb, he says the תמורה works.

keyTerms.meaning: But not (marking the limit of a ruling)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
One may substitute limbs for whole animals,
but not whole animals for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְמִירִין אֵבָרִים בִּשְׁלֵימִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about one case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-holy limb exchanged for a whole holy animal becomes a תמורה; a whole animal exchanged for a holy limb does not.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's proof from consecrating a leg
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי proves his view from הקדש: if you call one leg of an animal an עולה, the whole animal becomes an עולה, so naming one leg as a תמורה should make the whole animal a תמורה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי argues: when a person says 'this animal's leg is an עולה,' the whole animal becomes an עולה. So when he says 'this animal's leg is in place of that one,' the whole animal should become a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up his opinion by comparing it to a known rule about making something holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The known rule is that holiness given to one limb spreads to the whole animal. רבי יוסי says תמורה works the same way: the limb is just a way of naming the animal, so the whole animal becomes the substitute.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? (introducing a proof)
Animals made holy for the בית המקדש
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
A substitute animal that becomes holy through an exchange

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי's proof is about naming a limb of the ordinary animal. That is the direction he allows: a limb exchanged for a whole holy animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
But isn't it so with consecrated animals,
that one who says, "The leg of this one is a burnt offering" —
the whole animal is a burnt offering?

phrases.aramaic: אַף כְּשֶׁיֹּאמַר ״רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ תַּחַת זוֹ״
phrases.english: So too, when he says, "The leg of this one is in place of that one,"
the whole animal should be a substitute in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁין, הָאוֹמֵר רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוסי's opinion in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's ruling that a limb can be exchanged for a whole holy animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that making one leg of an animal an עולה makes the whole animal an עולה.

steps.title: Does holiness take hold of a fetus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a מחלוקת: בר פדא says קדושה does not take effect on a fetus, and רבי יוחנן says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא says you cannot make an unborn fetus holy. רבי יוחנן says you can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by bringing an argument about whether a fetus can become holy at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said fetuses cannot be used in a תמורה. This raises a more basic question: can a fetus receive holiness in the first place? בר פדא says no. רבי יוחנן says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness takes effect on something
Holiness does not take effect

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was stated: Bar Padda says:
Holiness does not take effect on fetuses,
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Holiness does take effect on fetuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, בַּר פְּדָא אָמַר: אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל עוּבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's ruling about fetuses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר פדא: a fetus cannot become holy on its own. רבי יוחנן: a fetus can become holy.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: the pregnant sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's view matches another ruling of his. If a pregnant animal was made a חטאת and gave birth, the owner may use either the mother or the baby for atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits רבי יוחנן's other ruling: if someone made a pregnant animal a חטאת and it gave birth, he can bring either the mother or the baby to get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's view here fits a ruling he gave elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby can serve as the חטאת only if it became holy as a חטאת in its own right while it was still a fetus. So this ruling assumes that קדושה takes effect on a fetus, exactly as רבי יוחנן said in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own line of reasoning (is consistent)
A sin offering
Pregnant
Gets atonement

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If one consecrated a pregnant animal as a sin offering and it gave birth —
if he wishes, he gets atonement through the mother;
if he wishes, he gets atonement through its offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוחנן's opinion in step 18 matches another ruling of his.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that קדושה takes effect on a fetus.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the offspring of a pregnant חטאת can itself be brought for atonement.

steps.title: Both of רבי יוחנן's rulings are needed: starting with the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a צריכותא, an explanation of why both of רבי יוחנן's rulings about a fetus are necessary. It begins with the first ruling, where a person makes the fetus itself holy. One could think the fetus becomes holy there only because he named it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both statements are needed. If רבי יוחנן had only taught us the first case, I would have said that only there does the fetus become holy, because he made it holy...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up an explanation of why רבי יוחנן needed to say two rulings that seem to teach the same thing. This line is not finished yet: it starts the reasoning, and the next part completes the thought and turns to the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, רבי יוחנן said a fetus can receive קדושה, and in step 19 we saw his ruling that the baby of a pregnant חטאת can be used for atonement. Both seem to say that קדושה works on a fetus, so the גמרא shows each one teaches something new. Here it starts by suggesting that from the first case alone, we might think the fetus becomes holy only because the owner made it holy directly and on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed. This is the opening word of a צריכותא, which explains why two similar teachings are both necessary.
He taught us, or he let us hear.
That first one, meaning the first case or ruling mentioned.
He made it holy, or he consecrated it.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether רבי יוחנן is right. It accepts both of his rulings and is only explaining why he needed to state both of them.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: Meaning: both of רבי יוחנן's rulings are needed, even though they look alike.

phrases.english: for if he had taught us only that first case
phrases.notes: The first case is the one from step 18, where someone makes the fetus itself holy.

phrases.english: I would say that only there it is holy, because he consecrated it

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing in step 19 that רבי יוחנן has a second ruling matching his view, the גמרא explains why both rulings are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both of רבי יוחנן's rulings are necessary. From the first case alone, one could think the fetus becomes holy only because it was directly consecrated.
